command:
set -e

# ONLY IF ABSENT. Regenerating on every `up` would invalidate every
# token already issued, so a running demo would start answering 401 for
# no visible reason.
if [ -f /app/services/auth/keys/private.pem ]; then
  echo "setup: signing keypair already present, keeping it"
else
  echo "setup: generating the JWT signing keypair"
  cd /app/services/auth && node scripts/generate-keys.mjs && cd /app
fi

# ONLY THE PUBLIC HALF LEAVES jwt-keys. Every service that verifies a token
# mounts jwt-public instead. They used to mount jwt-keys itself, read-only,
# with private.pem at 0600 -- which kept out nobody, because every container
# runs as the same `node` user that owns the file. scripts/verify-key-custody.mjs
# asserts it from inside each container. Copied on every run, so a
# regenerated keypair cannot leave a stale public key behind.
cp /app/services/auth/keys/public.pem /app/public-keys/public.pem

# Notification's keypair, which Auth seals email requests to. The script
# keeps an existing keypair, and on every run copies ONLY the public half
# into jwt-keys, where Auth reads it. The private half stays in
# notification-keys, which nothing but Notification will mount.
echo "setup: Notification's keypair"
node /app/services/notification/scripts/generate-keys.mjs

echo "setup: migrating auth"
DATABASE_URL="$$AUTH_DATABASE_URL" pnpm --filter @eventhub/auth exec prisma migrate deploy
echo "setup: migrating event"
DATABASE_URL="$$EVENT_DATABASE_URL" pnpm --filter @eventhub/event exec prisma migrate deploy
echo "setup: migrating ticketing"
DATABASE_URL="$$TICKETING_DATABASE_URL" pnpm --filter @eventhub/ticketing exec prisma migrate deploy
echo "setup: migrating live"
DATABASE_URL="$$LIVE_DATABASE_URL" pnpm --filter @eventhub/live exec prisma migrate deploy
echo "setup: migrating notification"
DATABASE_URL="$$NOTIFICATION_DATABASE_URL" pnpm --filter @eventhub/notification exec prisma migrate deploy
echo "setup: migrating community"
DATABASE_URL="$$COMMUNITY_DATABASE_URL" pnpm --filter @eventhub/community exec prisma migrate deploy

# Auth only. Every service's prisma.config.ts declares the same seed
# command and only Auth has the file, so running this against the others
# dies on a missing module.
echo "setup: seeding auth"
DATABASE_URL="$$AUTH_DATABASE_URL" pnpm --filter @eventhub/auth exec prisma db seed

# Seeded users get no card from /register, so they are queued here. Only
# users who never had one, and users whose card was not made under their
# tenant's current slug -- every card from before cards named the tenant's
# subdomain, which Notification needs for a reply's link. A second `up`
# queues nothing.
#
# PORT is given although the command listens on nothing: Auth's db.ts validates
# the whole base environment, and PORT has no default there. Without it the
# command died with "PORT: Expected number, received nan" — in this job only,
# because the verifier runs it with Auth's full environment.
echo "setup: queueing contact cards"
PORT=3001 DATABASE_URL="$$AUTH_DATABASE_URL" APP_DATABASE_URL="$$AUTH_APP_DATABASE_URL" pnpm --filter @eventhub/auth run contact-cards:publish

# Not optional: the broker runs with KAFKA_AUTO_CREATE_TOPICS_ENABLE=false
# on purpose, so nothing will create these on first publish.
echo "setup: creating topics"
node scripts/create-topics.mjs
echo "setup: registering Avro schemas"
node scripts/register-schemas.mjs

# From index-definition.ts, before the indexer can write anything. Needs
# only OPENSEARCH_NODE, set above: the script reads cluster-env.ts.
echo "setup: creating the search index"
pnpm --filter @eventhub/search run bootstrap:index

# Idempotent, and refuses a migration edited after it was applied.
echo "setup: migrating analytics"
pnpm --filter @eventhub/analytics run migrate

echo "setup: done"
